summary: Russia launched a massive coordinated missile and drone strike across Ukraine on Independence Day, hitting Kyiv, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Chernihiv, Poltava, and Kremenchuk, causing multiple casualties and infrastructure damage. Ukrainian officials acknowledge a critical shortage of air defense missiles extending beyond Patriot systems. Japan and South Korea have refused to supply Patriot interceptor missiles, while European leaders plan a U.S. visit to lobby for additional air defense support.
key_points: Russian strikes hit at least seven Ukrainian regions on Independence Day, including Kyiv, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Chernihiv, Poltava, and Kremenchuk, with reported deaths and injuries. (Source: @UkraineNow/83672)
Ukrainian Air Force spokesman Yuriy Ignat confirmed a missile shortage affecting not only Patriot but other ground-based air defense systems and aircraft. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32707)
Japan's Cabinet Secretary stated Tokyo is not considering arms supplies to Kyiv; South Korea similarly refused Patriot missile transfers. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32709)
European leaders plan to travel to the U.S. to persuade Donald Trump to provide Ukraine with Patriot missiles. (Source: @UkraineNow/83674)
Russian BARS-Kursk unit shot down an FP-5 Flamingo rocket targeting a strategic facility in Tula region using a machine gun. (Source: @tass_agency/391866)

Romania's Arsenal Resita plant, operated by UK-based Tor International, produces 25,000 155mm rounds and 20,000 propellant bags monthly under contracts with the U.S. Pentagon and Brazil. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32696)
The Economist reports systemic corruption in Ukraine is now treated as routine, posing the strongest challenge yet to Zelensky's leadership. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32704)
Paul Houston appointed new head of U.S. Embassy in Ukraine, replacing Sandra Oudkirk after just over a month. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32694)

sections.executive_summary: Russia conducted a large-scale missile and drone barrage across Ukraine on Independence Day, striking at least seven regions including Kyiv, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Chernihiv, Poltava, and Kremenchuk, resulting in multiple fatalities and injuries. Ukrainian air defense capabilities are severely degraded, with officials admitting shortages of interceptors for Patriot and other systems. Meanwhile, key allies Japan and South Korea have declined to provide Patriot missiles, while European leaders prepare a diplomatic push in Washington to secure additional air defense assets.

sections.threat_assessment: Russia's demonstrated ability to conduct simultaneous multi-axis strikes using diverse missile and drone types across a broad geographic area indicates sustained high-intensity strike capacity and improved coordination. Ukraine's acknowledged interceptor shortage, combined with allied refusal to supply Patriot missiles, creates a widening air defense gap that Russia can exploit with continued massed attacks. The targeting of civilian infrastructure (shopping centers, residential buildings) alongside industrial and military sites suggests a deliberate strategy to degrade societal resilience and defense production. The successful Russian shootdown of an FP-5 Flamingo rocket over Tula region reveals growing domestic air defense proficiency, potentially complicating future Ukrainian long-range strike planning.
